The WPF window collects input. ADO.NET sends SQL to SQL Server and returns the rows to the list on the screen.

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

Prepare and run

This WPF project needs Windows and the .NET desktop development workload. First run setup.sql from project 05-ado-sqlserver in SSMS. Change the local SQL connection if your instance is different, or set STUDYLAB_SQL in the launching environment. Open the desktop project and select ADO.NET SQL Server in the dropdown. Enter Name and Age. Use Create, Read, Update selected and Delete selected.

Trace one button

Create validates the form, opens a SqlConnection, creates an INSERT SqlCommand, adds typed parameters and calls ExecuteNonQuery. Read runs SELECT and loops over SqlDataReader. Selecting a row copies its values into the text boxes. Update/Delete use that selected ID. using closes connections/readers promptly. The simple synchronous desktop handlers are intentionally small; a larger application should use asynchronous I/O to keep the UI responsive.

Expected behaviour

Create Lefa,22 then Read: Lefa appears. Select it, change age to 23, choose Update selected, then Read: age is 23 when selected again. Delete selected removes the row. Invalid input displays a message. SQL errors are shown locally for this lab, not sent to public clients.

Try it yourself

Click Update selected with no row selected.

Worked answer

Expected: Select a student. Do not invent an ID from a text box without validating its relationship to the selected record.

Which parts change when moving this repository to an API?

Worked answer

The SQL access rules remain similar. Replace WPF events with HTTP endpoints, scoped services, async methods and safe response/error handling.
